assessment: The incumbent supports telephone/in-person reservations and staffed key collection; eleven groups obtained weekly bookings (H4-O1). Success is unestablished: total needs are unknown, three conflicts occurred, and administration averaged 127.5 minutes weekly (H4-O4, H4-O6). A plausible account is that useful access depends on matching timing/equipment and reliably communicating changes. The concrete limiting observation is six declined requests concentrated on Tuesday/Thursday evenings (H4-O3): 68% aggregate reservation occupancy (H4-O2) does not demonstrate spare capacity within acceptable windows. Late or missed bookings likewise do not establish recoverable rehearsal time.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: one authoritative desk booking ledger, with uniquely identified reservations and read-back confirmation of changes, can reduce conflicting expectations while preserving phone and in-person access; the online copy would show when it was last synchronized.
openings.delta: Makes reservation state and change acknowledgment explicit within the existing volunteer/desk workflow.
openings.prediction: If divergent records or unacknowledged changes cause conflicts, discrepancies and duplicate room expectations should decrease; added confirmation work could instead worsen administrative load.
openings.probe: Trial within existing staffing: log each change once, confirm room/date/time verbally, and track copy discrepancies, conflicting arrivals, and total weekly administration. Judge the eight-week conflict and average-time targets directly.
assumptions: The desk and volunteer can share an authoritative ledger using existing resources.
Some conflicting expectations originate in recording or communication; the causes of two observed conflicts remain unknown.

openings.claim: Can existing rooms and hours satisfy at least 90% of stated rehearsal needs once acceptable windows, required duration, and equipment are recorded, with every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement protected?
openings.delta: Distinguishes a feasible allocation obscured by inherited bookings from a binding time/equipment bottleneck.
openings.prediction: A feasible schedule supports testing reallocation; a demonstrated unavoidable shortfall identifies a bottleneck that aggregate vacancy conceals. Failure to find a schedule alone would not prove infeasibility.
openings.probe: Use the short contact conversations to record needs and all acceptable alternatives, then construct a paper eight-week allocation with performances fixed, existing equipment/hours, and weekly entitlements protected. Count outside rehearsals only when their suitability and dependable access are confirmed.
assumptions: Contacts can report their groups' needs and acceptable alternatives accurately.
A 60-minute entitlement is a minimum, not evidence that it fulfills a group's entire need.
